name: Slavic Lang & Lit (Min)

rules.name: Preparing for the Minor
rules.desc:
Students interested in Slavic Languages and Literatures Russian Language subplan should begin by taking first-year or taking the Language Center placement examination for a Slavic language to demonstrate their fluency. First-Year language coursework (RUSSLANG 1, 2, & 3, or 1A & 2A, or equivalent) are prerequisites, and will not count toward the minor units requirement.
Early in their studies, it is recommended that students take introductory courses in literature, language, or the humanities to build a foundation in literary traditions, theory, and languages.
To plan their course of study, including electives and any thematic or regional focus, students should consult the department's Program Worksheet, available from the DLCL Undergraduate Student Services Officer, and discuss it with the Director of Undergraduate Studies (DUS).

children.name: Russian Language
children.desc: Students must complete three Intermediate Russian Language courses.
children.notes: First-Year Russian will not count toward the minor unit requirement.

children.name: Elective Courses
children.desc: Students must enroll in at least three SLAVIC courses to meet the degree course and unit minimums, or, with the approval of the department's Director of Undergraduate Studies, elective courses in History, Politics, Linguistics, or other relevant programs.

children.name: At least six courses of 3 units or more

grading: All courses must be taken for a letter grade, except where letter grades are not offered.
policies: These 24 units may not be used toward any other major or minor.
transferPolicy: Transfer and AP credit are not accepted.
reviewNotes: You choose Russian Language (three intermediate Russian courses and at least three SLAVIC courses) or Russian Language, Literature, and Culture (three of SLAVIC 145-148 and more SLAVIC courses), at least six courses of 3 units or more and 24 units in all, letter graded where a letter grade is offered. First-year Russian does not count, and approved courses from other departments are moved in by hand. The units cannot count toward another major or minor, and transfer and AP credit are not accepted; you check those yourself.
